# WO-2026-08-18-01 — the suggestions are catalogue noise

**A live weekly shop is BLOCKED and Warwick is rightly angry.** His words:

> *"these questions make no fucking sense and the formatting is horrible and not human readable… Asdair is
> supposed to be dealing with this shit… not me. He can't be, there is no way these suggestions came from
> something intelligent or something that has read the rules"*

**He is right, and it is NOT a model failure — it is a ranking bug visible in the source.**

## What he was actually offered

| he wrote | AsdAIr suggested |
|---|---|
| `1 x 4pk Ben & Jerrys cookie dough` | **ASDA 4 Beef Quarter Pounders**, Twix ice cream |
| `1 wet wipes` | **Gourmet Wet CAT FOOD** |
| `2 pkts ASDA plain toffees` | **ham · eggs · freezer bags · quarter pounders · bananas** |
| `1 pk. ASDA fruit lolly ices` | **ham · apple slices · eggs · freezer bags · quarter pounders** |

## THE MECHANISM — established by reading the source, not guessed

`services/asdair/skill/planner.js:262`

```js
const words = term.split(' ').filter(function (w) { return w.length > 2; });
```

**The ONLY filter is word length.** So `asda` — a token carried by a large share of the catalogue — scores
`1/4 = 0.25`, passes the `if (best === 0) return;` guard, and the tie-break at `:301` is **alphabetical by
name**. **That is exactly the list he saw: `ASDA 10…`, `ASDA 12…`, `ASDA 20…`, `ASDA 4…`, `ASDA 6…`.**
Same mechanism elsewhere: `wet` → *Wet Cat Food*; `4pk` → *Twix … 4pk*.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — low-information tokens must not qualify a candidate on their own.** Store and brand words carried
across a large share of the catalogue (`asda` being the obvious one), pack and unit tokens (`pkt`, `pkts`,
`pk`, `4pk`, `x`, `g`, `kg`, `ml`, `ltr`) and bare numbers. **Prefer deriving the suppression FROM THE
CATALOGUE — a term appearing in more than some share of rows carries no information — over hand-maintaining
a word list.** State the threshold you chose and why.

**AC2 — ⛔ AN EMPTY CANDIDATE LIST IS A CORRECT ANSWER. This is the heart of the order.** Below a minimum
score, offer **NOTHING** and say so plainly. **A wrong suggestion is worse than no suggestion** — it wastes
his attention and invites a mis-tap that first-answer-wins then makes permanent. **Prove by execution that
at least one of the seven yields an EMPTY list rather than filler.**

**AC3 — prove it on the REAL seven.** Against the **real 109-row catalogue**, show before/after for every
one: `2 sliced roast beef` · `Heinz Tinned Baked Beans 6 x 415g` · `1 x 4pk Ben & Jerrys cookie dough` ·
`1 pk. ASDA fruit lolly ices` · `1 wet wipes` · `2 Sure deoderent male` · `2 pkts ASDA plain toffees`.
**Every surviving candidate must share a MEANINGFUL term with the reading. Paste the table.**

**AC4 — the Sure deodorants are the case that SHOULD still offer candidates.** All four Sure variants are
genuinely plausible for *"2 Sure deoderent male"*. **Do not over-suppress into uselessness** — this is the
control proving the fix did not simply turn everything off.

**AC5 — ⛔ WHY IS AN ALREADY-MATCHED LINE BEING ASKED ABOUT?** Question 2 quotes a **full catalogue name**
back at him — `Heinz Tinned Baked Beans in a Rich Tomato Sauce 6 x 415g` — with **no candidates at all**,
and the raw reading `1 x 6pk Heinz baked beans` had **already matched regular id 108**. **Establish why a
resolved line produced a question. Report it. Fix it ONLY if the cause is inside your surface** — if it is
upstream, name the file and stop.

**AC6 — the card is not human-readable**, and that is Warwick's second complaint, separate from the
ranking. `questionRender.js`. **He reads this on a phone.** Fix what is genuinely unreadable — the wall of
semicolon-separated 60-character catalogue names is the main offender — **without inventing a format
language or a template engine.** One candidate per line, and the **`display_name`** where one exists rather
than the retailer string.

## Required evidence

- `cd services/asdair/skill && node --test` and `cd services/asdair/bot && node --test` → real counts.
- **The AC3 before/after table against the real catalogue.** This is the one that matters.
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface <your paths>` → exit code AND coverage.

## Explicitly out of scope — report, never fix

- **The answer-binding defect** (answers landing one row off) and **first-answer-wins being uncorrectable**
  — recorded in `Deliverables/2026-08-17-b15-5-real-run-defects.md`. **Real, open, NOT this order.**
- **Terra's intermittent invention.** Same file, same rule.
- **The live shop itself. Larry handles anything touching `SHOP-2026-08-18-M128`.**

## Sequencing

**READ-BACK AND HOLD — keep it SHORT, a live shop is blocked.** Then AC1 → AC2 → AC3 → AC4 → AC5 → AC6.
Commit on `build-015/b15-54-candidate-quality` in `C:/Fusion247PKA-planner` and push. No PR, no merge.

**Proportion: this is a hobby brain, not enterprise search.** The goal is *"a human would find these
plausible"* — not a relevance engine. **If you find yourself building a scoring framework, stop.**
